subject: Streaming emit latency — interim notice, mitigation steps, and next actions
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Navarro <alex@harbortech.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Streaming emit latency — interim update and a short mitigation ask

Alex —

Thanks for the quick call earlier. We’ve confirmed HarborTech is seeing increased tail latency on streaming/chat responses starting ~14:50 UTC and persisting through the hour. Brief summary up front:

- Impact: elevated per-token latency and occasional stall >5s for a subset of interactive sessions (primarily models with long user prefixes).
- Scope: ~4% of active sessions routed to the EU-edge cluster we rolled out a kernel tweak to this morning.
- Immediate mitigation in-flight: routing throttles and a targeted rollback to the previous kernel selection are underway; we expect measurable improvement within 30–45 minutes.

What we need from you now (short ask):
1) If you can temporarily reduce concurrent message streaming concurrency from your front-end (from current 8 -> 3) for the next 60 minutes, it will reduce pressure on our edge proxies and accelerate recovery.
2) If possible, identify any very long static prefixes in requests (logs reference prefixes >8k tokens) and pause batching those for now — our KV cache misses on long prefixes are amplifying CPU fallbacks.

Attachments: brief diagnostics bundle attached (diagnostics_snapshot_20260930.zip) and a small suggested config patch to reduce edge thread pool size as a short-term pressure relief (config_suggestion_patch.diff).

We’ll send a follow-up when the rollback completes and share a remediation plan and postmortem timeline. Sorry for the disruption — we know this impacts your user experience.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0173

From: Alex Navarro <alex@harbortech.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 15:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Streaming emit latency — interim update and a short mitigation ask

Thanks Mateo —

We appreciate the quick triage. We are already seeing user complaints on the dashboard and some timeouts on our websocket client. I’ve pushed a deploy to reduce concurrency to 3 (rolling out now).

A couple quick asks from our side:
- ETA on the rollback completing? Can you confirm whether this will require a restart of our dedicated pool or is it a transparent kernel reselect?
- We’ll scan for long prefixes but can you point to the best log keys to search so we don’t miss anything?

Also — please confirm whether you plan to issue a credit for impacted minutes. Our product team will want that noted for the post-incident review.

— Alex
Alex Navarro
Head of Platform Engineering, HarborTech
alex@harbortech.com

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Alex Navarro <alex@harbortech.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Streaming emit latency — interim update and a short mitigation ask

Laura / Ben —

Forwarding HarborTech thread — we’ve got the customer reducing concurrency as requested. Current internal status:

- Root cause (preliminary): a kernel selection change pushed to EU-edge this morning caused higher CPU fallback rates when KV cache miss ratios spiked for long-prefix requests. That fallback path increases per-token CPU latency and interacts poorly with our continuous batching heuristics, producing the stutters.
- Short-term actions in flight: rollback kernel selection on the affected shard (no customer restart required), reduce edge thread-pool size on eu-edge to reduce contention, and increase client-side socket timeouts for streaming (we suggested the concurrency change to HarborTech).
- Observable metric to watch: token_emit_latency.p95 and kv_cache_miss_rate. I attached a diagnostics bundle and config patch.

Action items I need your help with ASAP:
1) Ben: confirm credit proposal (minutes impacted estimate below) and prepare a short note for legal/finance. I estimate 7–12k affected minutes across HarborTech sessions during the window; more accurate numbers after we process the log bundle.
2) Laura: schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with HarborTech engineers for tomorrow (I suggested 09:30 UTC) to walk through root cause, mitigations, and permanent fixes.
3) Both: we should prepare an interim incident slide deck for the customer and a public-facing postmortem within 72 hours.

I’ll update this thread as rollback completes.

— Mateo

Attachments: diagnostics_snapshot_20260930.zip, config_suggestion_patch.diff
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Alex Navarro <alex@harbortech.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 18:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Streaming emit latency — interim update and a short mitigation ask

Thanks Mateo — and thanks Alex for the quick reaction on your side.

Update and next steps:
- The rollback completed at 17:40 UTC and we saw token_emit_latency.p95 drop ~65% on the affected shard within 10 minutes. HarborTech’s telemetry confirms improved client-side behavior.
- We will compile a postmortem and an incident slide deck; draft delivery to HarborTech: 2026-10-02 09:30 UTC (technical deep-dive meeting), public postmortem: 2026-10-03 EOD.
- Credits: Ben, please prepare a credit proposal equal to the impacted usage minutes (est. 8,900) and include a one-time account credit and a waived overage for this billing cycle.

Permanent remediation plan (high level):
1) Revert kernel selection change from this morning and add a staged canary with heavier KV-miss synthetic load before rollout.
2) Improve the continuous-batching heuristics to detect CPU-fallback-induced jitter and temporarily revert to a smaller batch size when emit latency crosses a threshold.
3) Add an alert and automatic short-circuit routing policy that moves affected sessions to a lower-latency pool while the shard recovers.

We’ll follow up with the incident slide deck (attached: incident_slides_20260930.pdf) and a conformed timeline. Mateo — please coordinate the deep-dive invite with Alex for 09:30 UTC on 2026-10-02.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
